id: # lane/enddiv: lane/dragon's dragon kill (seed 2's env 2 of dragon_case from gold-g30-s42, its tape on the Java client from checkpoint 42/G29) replayed by the C engine row for row; the Java run is end-kill-g30-s42 (24,000 rows, the kill and the exit portal at 21,353)

cause: the End's crystal slots (dragon.h DRAGON_MAX_CRYSTALS, 64) were never given back: every chunk reload of a spike constructs a new EntityEnderCrystal and took a new slot, the unloaded one kept; a long fight around the island ran out at row 5747 and two saved crystals of a reloaded chunk were never constructed (Java 134 entities, C 132; every later id two lower). dragon_crystal_slot reuses a slot whose crystal left the world, except the dragon's healingEnderCrystal

an arrow a chunk reload rebuilt (sr_arrow_adopt) joined only the living world's chunk sections: ie_added_to_world adds nothing while the chunk being read is not yet in the world, and the player's pickup walk (EntityPlayer.onLivingUpdate, collide_with_player_pool) reads the item world's, so the player never picked it up (row 5995: Java's slot 20 arrows 30 to 31, C 30). It now joins the chunk as Chunk.addEntity does (ie_add_to_chunk, as sr_restore_tnt)

the oracle's client keeps a fire the server cleared on a destroyed crystal's spike: the blast's S27 clears the client's fire, the flush's S23 sends the server's air, then the crystal's client copy (EntityEnderCrystal.onUpdate runs on the client, and in the End puts fire in its cell) writes it back before its S13 a tick later. C untracked a crystal at setDead (pickobj view_of), a tick before World.updateEntities removes it, and its copy wrote no fire, so its client world had air where the void fog's thousand samples read fire (the dragon kill's second tape, row 11251: 6893 client Random steps against Java's 6891).
